terms.gloss: go on strike (literally, break off work)
evidence: Caes. BG 3.29: opus (Lewis & Short s.v. intermittō)
terms.comment: To break off work: Caesar’s phrase for halting the work of a siege or a camp (Lewis & Short). Used of a strike it is Traupman’s; the Latin does not itself say that the stoppage is a protest.
A modern coinage on the model of jūstitium, the suspension of the courts; not in Lewis & Short.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 386.
